title: Windows Where the Ends Are Half the Middle
statement:
You get an integer array nums. Look at every window of three consecutive values nums[i], nums[i + 1], nums[i + 2]. A window is balanced when the sum of its two outer values equals exactly half of its middle value.

Return how many balanced windows there are. Windows overlap: each start index i gives its own window. Half of an odd number is not a whole number, so an odd middle can never be matched.

examples.why: Half of 3 is 1.5, not 1. Integer division would say 3 / 2 = 1 and count it by mistake.
Two overlapping windows, both 0 + 0 = half of 0.

hints: How many windows of length 3 does an array of length n have?
Comparing with half of the middle invites rounding bugs. Can you compare whole numbers only?
a + c equals b / 2 exactly when 2 · (a + c) equals b. Check that for every start index.

explain.intuition:
The window has a fixed size, so there is nothing to grow or shrink: slide a length-3 frame from index 0 to index n − 3 and test each one. That is n − 2 windows.

The real trap is the division. In most languages b / 2 on integers rounds, and rounding turns 3 into 1 or −1 into 0 (JavaScript gives 1.5 and −0.5, but many people reach for Math.floor or >> 1). Multiply instead: a + c = b / 2 is the same as 2 · (a + c) = b, and that is exact with whole numbers.
steps: For i from 0 to n − 3: let a = nums[i], b = nums[i + 1], c = nums[i + 2].
If 2 · (a + c) === b, add one to count.
pitfalls: Using integer division for half of the middle. [0, 3, 1] and [0, -1, 0] are then counted by mistake.
Looping to n − 2 or n − 1 and reading past the end of the array.
Skipping ahead by 3 after a match. Windows overlap, so every start index needs its own check.

solutions.title: Slide a length-3 frame, compare without dividing
solutions.idea: Check 2 · (a + c) === b at every start index.

followups: Windows can have any length k ≥ 3: the two ends must sum to half of the sum of everything strictly between them. How do prefix sums keep each check O(1)?
Return the start indices of the balanced windows instead of the count.
